intro: っけ is the particle of a half-remembered fact. You knew it once, it has slipped away, and you are fishing for it, either in your own memory or from the listener: 'what was it again?'. It never asks about something new.

skills.rule: End with だっけ or past-tense たっけ when you are trying to recall something you once knew: 'what was ... again?', 'did I ...?'.
skills.explain:
Use っけ for a fact that has slipped your mind: あの人の名前、何だっけ？ 'what's his name again?'; 会議は何時からだっけ？ 'what time does the meeting start again?'. Said to someone, it is a light question; muttered, it is you searching your memory. 言ったっけ？ means 'did I tell you?'.

っけ attaches after だ, だった or a past-tense た: 何だっけ, 何だったっけ, 行ったっけ. A present-tense verb normally goes through んだ: 明日来るんだっけ？ 'you're coming tomorrow, aren't you?'. Bare 来るっけ is heard in casual speech, but んだっけ is the safe form. A noun with no だ (何っけ) is wrong. Polite forms are common and natural: お名前は何でしたっけ, もう払いましたっけ.

It presupposes that you once knew. Asking a stranger's name with っけ tells them you have forgotten it. In older or reflective style, past + っけ also looks back fondly: 子どもの頃、よくここで遊んだっけ, 'I used to play here a lot as a kid'.
patterns: でしたっけ / ましたっけ  (polite)

examples.jp: 今日[きょう]は何曜日[なんようび]だ{っけ}？
examples.en: What day is it today again?

examples.jp: あの人[ひと]の名前[なまえ]、何[なん]だった{っけ}？
examples.en: What was that person's name again?

examples.jp: この話[はなし]、もう言[い]った{っけ}？
examples.en: Have I told you this already?

examples.jp: 会議[かいぎ]は何時[なんじ]からでした{っけ}。
examples.en: What time does the meeting start again?

examples.jp: 田中[たなか]さんは明日[あした]来[く]るんだ{っけ}？
examples.en: Tanaka's coming tomorrow, right? I forget.

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもの頃[ころ]、よくこの川[かわ]で泳[およ]いだ{っけ}。
examples.en: When I was a kid, I used to swim in this river a lot.

contrast.note: かな wonders about something unknown, often in the future: 明日晴れるかな. っけ recovers something known: 明日は何曜日だっけ.
よね checks a fact you are fairly sure of: 会議は三時からだよね. っけ admits you have lost it: 会議は何時からだっけ.
か asks for new information: お名前は何ですか, on first meeting. お名前は何でしたっけ says you were told and have forgotten.

mistakes.bad: 今日[きょう]は何曜日[なんようび]{っけ}？
mistakes.good: 今日[きょう]は何曜日[なんようび]だ{っけ}？
mistakes.note: A noun needs だ (or でした) before っけ.

mistakes.bad: （'I wonder if it'll rain tomorrow.'）明日[あした]は雨[あめ]が降[ふ]る{っけ}。
mistakes.good: （'I wonder if it'll rain tomorrow.'）明日[あした]は雨[あめ]が降[ふ]る{かな}。
mistakes.note: Nobody told you tomorrow's weather, so there is nothing to recall. Wondering about the unknown takes かな.

mistakes.bad: （初[はじ]めて会[あ]った人[ひと]に）お名前[なまえ]は何[なん]でした{っけ}。
mistakes.good: （初[はじ]めて会[あ]った人[ひと]に）お名前[なまえ]は何[なん]です{か}。
mistakes.note: You were never told this person's name, so there is nothing to recall: ask with か.

skills.tip: Does the English need 'again' ('what was it again?')? Then っけ.
